9	### Conjugation and normality
10	
11	This is the [Classical.Structures.Group.Conjugation][] module of the [Agda Universal Algebra Library][].
12	
13	For a group `𝑮`{.AgdaBound} this module develops conjugation — first of elements
14	(`conj g x = g ∙ x ∙ g ⁻¹`), then of subgroups — and the normality predicate, the
15	ingredients from which [Classical.Structures.Group.NormalCore][] builds the normal
16	core `Core_G(H)` as a complete-lattice meet.
17	
18	Two design points deserve comment.
19	
20	+  **The conjugate of a subgroup is defined as an image, not a preimage**.  We take
21	   `conjugate g B = { x ∣ ∃ h ∈ B , x ≈ conj g h }`, the ≈-saturated image of `B`
22	   under `conj g`, rather than the preimage `{ x ∣ conj (g ⁻¹) x ∈ B }`.  Over a
23	   setoid carrier the image form is superior: it respects the setoid equality *by
24	   construction* (no hypothesis on `B` needed), and it is a subuniverse whenever `B`
25	   is a bare subuniverse.  For equality-respecting `B` the two forms agree.
26	+  **Normality is the pointwise property** `∀ g x → x ∈ B → conj g x ∈ B`.  The
27	   bridge lemmas `normal-conjugate-⊆`{.AgdaFunction} and
28	   `normal-⊆-conjugate`{.AgdaFunction} recover the equivalent formulation "every
29	   conjugate of `B` coincides with `B`" when `B` respects the equality.
30	
31	All proofs are small equational chains over the group axioms; the derived
32	cancellation laws (`\\-leftDividesʳ` and friends) come from the standard library's
33	`Algebra.Properties.Group`{.AgdaModule} applied to the bundle view
34	`⟨ 𝑮 ⟩ᵍᵖ`{.AgdaFunction} of [Classical.Bundles.Group][], which is what the bundle
35	bridge exists for.
36	
37	<!--

44	
45	-- Imports from the Agda Standard Library ---------------------------------------

72	
73	#### Conjugation of elements
74	
75	`Conj 𝑮` packages conjugation in the group `𝑮`; opening it puts `conj`{.AgdaFunction}
76	and its algebra of laws in scope.  The laws say: conjugation by a fixed `g` is a group
77	endomorphism (`conj-ε`{.AgdaFunction}, `conj-∙-hom`{.AgdaFunction},
78	`conj-⁻¹`{.AgdaFunction}), and as `g` varies it is a left action of the group on
79	itself (`conj-action-ε`{.AgdaFunction}, `conj-action-∙`{.AgdaFunction}) by
80	≈-automorphisms (`conj-cong`{.AgdaFunction}, with `conj-conj⁻¹`{.AgdaFunction} and
81	`conj⁻¹-conj`{.AgdaFunction} the two inverse laws).
82	
83	```agda
84	module Conjugate {α ρ : Level} (𝒢@(𝑮 , eqns) : Group α ρ) where
85	
86	  open Setoid 𝔻[ 𝑮 ]  using ( _≈_ )
87	                      renaming ( refl to ≈refl ; sym to ≈sym ; trans to ≈trans )
88	  open SetoidReasoning 𝔻[ 𝑮 ]
89	  open Group-Op 𝒢 using ( _∙_ ; ε ; _⁻¹ ; ∙-cong ; ⁻¹-cong
90	                        ; assoc-law ; idˡ-law ; idʳ-law ; invˡ-law ; invʳ-law )
91	  open GroupProperties ⟨ 𝒢 ⟩ᵍᵖ
92	    using ( ε⁻¹≈ε ; ⁻¹-involutive ; ⁻¹-anti-homo-∙ ; \\-leftDividesʳ )
93	
94	  -- Conjugation of the element x by the element g.
95	  conj : 𝕌[ 𝑮 ] → 𝕌[ 𝑮 ] → 𝕌[ 𝑮 ]
96	  conj g x = g ∙ x ∙ g ⁻¹
97	
98	  infixl 30 conj-syntax
99	
100	  conj-syntax : 𝕌[ 𝑮 ] → 𝕌[ 𝑮 ] → 𝕌[ 𝑮 ]
101	  conj-syntax = conj
102	
103	  syntax conj-syntax g x = x ^ g
104	
105	  -- Conjugation is a congruence in the conjugated element ...
106	  conj-cong : ∀ g {x y} → x ≈ y → x ^ g ≈ y ^ g
107	  conj-cong g x≈y = ∙-cong (∙-cong ≈refl x≈y) ≈refl
108	
109	  -- ... and in the conjugating element.
110	  conj-congᵍ : ∀ {g h} x → g ≈ h → x ^ g ≈ x ^ h
111	  conj-congᵍ x g≈h = ∙-cong (∙-cong g≈h ≈refl) (⁻¹-cong g≈h)
112	
113	  -- Conjugation fixes the identity element.
114	  conj-ε : ∀ g → ε ^ g  ≈ ε
115	  conj-ε g = begin
116	    g ∙ ε ∙ g ⁻¹  ≈⟨ ∙-cong (idʳ-law g) ≈refl ⟩
117	    g ∙ g ⁻¹      ≈⟨ invʳ-law g ⟩
118	    ε             ∎
119	
120	  -- Conjugation by g is multiplicative.
121	  conj-∙-hom : ∀ g x y → (x ∙ y) ^ g ≈ (x ^ g) ∙ (y ^ g)
122	  conj-∙-hom g x y = begin
123	    (x ∙ y) ^ g                        ≈˘⟨ ∙-cong (assoc-law g x y) ≈refl ⟩
124	    g ∙ x ∙ y ∙ g ⁻¹                   ≈⟨ assoc-law (g ∙ x) y (g ⁻¹) ⟩
125	    g ∙ x ∙ (y ∙ g ⁻¹)                 ≈˘⟨ ∙-cong ≈refl (\\-leftDividesʳ g (y ∙ g ⁻¹)) ⟩
126	    g ∙ x ∙ (g ⁻¹ ∙ (g ∙ (y ∙ g ⁻¹)))  ≈˘⟨ ∙-cong ≈refl (∙-cong ≈refl (assoc-law g y (g ⁻¹))) ⟩
127	    g ∙ x ∙ (g ⁻¹ ∙ (y ^ g))           ≈˘⟨ assoc-law (g ∙ x) (g ⁻¹) (y ^ g) ⟩
128	    (x ^ g) ∙ (y ^ g)                  ∎
129	
130	  -- Conjugation by g commutes with inversion.
131	  conj-⁻¹ : ∀ g x → (x ⁻¹) ^ g ≈ (x ^ g) ⁻¹
132	  conj-⁻¹ g x = begin
133	    (x ⁻¹) ^ g              ≈⟨ assoc-law g (x ⁻¹) (g ⁻¹) ⟩
134	    g ∙ (x ⁻¹ ∙ g ⁻¹)       ≈˘⟨ ∙-cong (⁻¹-involutive g) (⁻¹-anti-homo-∙ g x) ⟩
135	    (g ⁻¹) ⁻¹ ∙ (g ∙ x) ⁻¹  ≈˘⟨ ⁻¹-anti-homo-∙ (g ∙ x) (g ⁻¹) ⟩
136	    (x ^ g) ⁻¹ ∎
137	
138	  -- Varying the conjugator: conjugation is a left action of the group on itself.
139	  conj-action-∙ : ∀ g h x → x ^ (g ∙ h) ≈ (x ^ h) ^ g
140	  conj-action-∙ g h x = begin
141	    x ^ (g ∙ h)                ≈⟨ ≈refl ⟩
142	    g ∙ h ∙ x ∙ (g ∙ h) ⁻¹     ≈⟨ ∙-cong ≈refl (⁻¹-anti-homo-∙ g h) ⟩
143	    g ∙ h ∙ x ∙ (h ⁻¹ ∙ g ⁻¹)  ≈˘⟨ assoc-law (g ∙ h ∙ x) (h ⁻¹) (g ⁻¹) ⟩
144	    g ∙ h ∙ x ∙ h ⁻¹ ∙ g ⁻¹    ≈⟨ ∙-cong (∙-cong (assoc-law g h x) ≈refl) ≈refl ⟩
145	    g ∙ (h ∙ x) ∙ h ⁻¹ ∙ g ⁻¹  ≈⟨ ∙-cong (assoc-law g (h ∙ x) (h ⁻¹)) ≈refl ⟩
146	    g ∙ (h ∙ x ∙ h ⁻¹) ∙ g ⁻¹  ≈⟨ ≈refl ⟩
147	    (x ^ h) ^ g  ∎
148	
149	  conj-action-ε : ∀ x → x ^ ε ≈ x
150	  conj-action-ε x = begin
151	    ε ∙ x ∙ ε ⁻¹  ≈⟨ ∙-cong (idˡ-law x) ε⁻¹≈ε ⟩
152	    x ∙ ε         ≈⟨ idʳ-law x ⟩
153	    x             ∎
154	
155	  -- Conjugating by g undoes conjugating by g ⁻¹, and vice versa.
156	  conj-conj⁻¹ : ∀ g x → x ^ (g ⁻¹) ^ g ≈ x
157	  conj-conj⁻¹ g x = begin
158	    x ^ (g ⁻¹) ^ g    ≈˘⟨ conj-action-∙ g (g ⁻¹) x ⟩
159	    x ^ (g ∙ g ⁻¹)    ≈⟨ conj-congᵍ x (invʳ-law g) ⟩
160	    x ^ ε             ≈⟨ conj-action-ε x ⟩
161	    x                 ∎
162	
163	  conj⁻¹-conj : ∀ g x → x ^ g ^ (g ⁻¹) ≈ x
164	  conj⁻¹-conj g x = begin
165	    x ^ g ^ (g ⁻¹)  ≈˘⟨ conj-action-∙ (g ⁻¹) g x ⟩
166	    x ^ (g ⁻¹ ∙ g)  ≈⟨ conj-congᵍ x (invˡ-law g) ⟩
167	    x ^ ε           ≈⟨ conj-action-ε x ⟩
168	    x               ∎
169	```
170	
171	#### Conjugation of subgroups
172	
173	The conjugate of a subset `B` by `g` is the ≈-saturated image of `B` under
174	`conj g`{.AgdaFunction}.  It respects the setoid equality by construction, and is a
175	subuniverse whenever `B` is (via the endomorphism laws above), so conjugation maps
176	subgroups to subgroups.
177	
178	```agda
179	  -- The conjugate subset g B g⁻¹.
180	  conjugate : 𝕌[ 𝑮 ] → Pred 𝕌[ 𝑮 ] ℓ → Pred 𝕌[ 𝑮 ] (α ⊔ ρ ⊔ ℓ)
181	  conjugate g B x = ∃[ h ] (h ∈ B × x ≈ h ^ g)
182	
183	  infixl 30 conjugate-syntax
184	
185	  conjugate-syntax : 𝕌[ 𝑮 ] → Pred 𝕌[ 𝑮 ] ℓ → Pred 𝕌[ 𝑮 ] (α ⊔ ρ ⊔ ℓ)
186	  conjugate-syntax = conjugate
187	
188	  syntax conjugate-syntax g B = [ B ]^ g
189	
190	  -- The conjugate respects the setoid equality, with no hypothesis on B.
191	  conjugate-respects : ∀ g (B : Pred 𝕌[ 𝑮 ] ℓ) → [ B ]^ g Respects _≈_
192	  conjugate-respects g B x≈y (h , h∈B , x≈c) = h , h∈B , ≈trans (≈sym x≈y) x≈c
193	
194	  -- Conjugation of an element lands in the conjugate of any subset containing it.
195	  mem-conjugate : ∀ g {B : Pred 𝕌[ 𝑮 ] ℓ} {x} → x ∈ B → x ^ g ∈ [ B ]^ g
196	  mem-conjugate g x∈B = _ , x∈B , ≈refl
197	
198	  -- Conjugation of subsets is monotone.
199	  conjugate-mono : ∀ g {B : Pred 𝕌[ 𝑮 ] ℓ} {C : Pred 𝕌[ 𝑮 ] ℓ'} → B ⊆ C → [ B ]^ g ⊆ [ C ]^ g
200	  conjugate-mono g B⊆C (h , h∈B , x≈c) = h , B⊆C h∈B , x≈c
201	
202	  -- The conjugate of a subuniverse is a subuniverse.
203	  conjugate-isSubuniverse : (g : 𝕌[ 𝑮 ]) (B : Pred 𝕌[ 𝑮 ] ℓ)
204	    →  B ∈ Subuniverses 𝑮 → [ B ]^ g ∈ Subuniverses 𝑮
205	  conjugate-isSubuniverse g B B-sub ∙-Op a im =
206	    h₀ ∙ h₁ , sub-∙-closed 𝒢 B B-sub h₀∈B h₁∈B , eq
207	    where
208	    h₀ h₁ : 𝕌[ 𝑮 ]
209	    h₀ = im 0F .proj₁
210	    h₁ = im 1F .proj₁
211	
212	    h₀∈B : h₀ ∈ B
213	    h₀∈B = im 0F .proj₂ .proj₁
214	
215	    h₁∈B : h₁ ∈ B
216	    h₁∈B = im 1F .proj₂ .proj₁
217	
218	    eq : (∙-Op ̂  𝑮) a ≈ (h₀ ∙ h₁) ^ g
219	    eq = begin
220	      (∙-Op ̂  𝑮) a      ≈⟨ interp-tuple-∙ 𝒢 a ⟩
221	      a 0F ∙ a 1F       ≈⟨ ∙-cong (im 0F .proj₂ .proj₂) (im 1F .proj₂ .proj₂) ⟩
222	      h₀ ^ g ∙ h₁ ^ g   ≈˘⟨ conj-∙-hom g h₀ h₁ ⟩
223	      (h₀ ∙ h₁) ^ g     ∎
224	
225	  conjugate-isSubuniverse g B B-sub ε-Op a im = ε , sub-ε-closed 𝒢 B B-sub , eq
226	    where
227	    eq : (ε-Op ̂  𝑮) a ≈ ε ^ g
228	    eq = begin
229	      (ε-Op ̂  𝑮) a  ≈⟨ interp-tuple-ε 𝒢 a ⟩
230	      ε             ≈˘⟨ conj-ε g ⟩
231	      ε ^ g         ∎
232	
233	  conjugate-isSubuniverse g B B-sub ⁻¹-Op a im = h ⁻¹ , sub-⁻¹-closed 𝒢 B B-sub h∈B , eq
234	    where
235	    h : 𝕌[ 𝑮 ]
236	    h = im 0F .proj₁
237	
238	    h∈B : h ∈ B
239	    h∈B = im 0F .proj₂ .proj₁
240	
241	    eq : (⁻¹-Op ̂  𝑮) a ≈ (h ⁻¹) ^ g
242	    eq = begin
243	      (⁻¹-Op ̂  𝑮) a  ≈⟨ interp-tuple-⁻¹ 𝒢 a ⟩
244	      a 0F ⁻¹        ≈⟨ ⁻¹-cong (im 0F .proj₂ .proj₂) ⟩
245	      (h ^ g) ⁻¹     ≈˘⟨ conj-⁻¹ g h ⟩
246	      (h ⁻¹) ^ g     ∎
247	```
248	
249	#### The normality predicate
250	
251	A subset is **normal** when it is closed under conjugation by every group element.
252	The property is stated for bare predicates; for ≈-respecting subgroups it is
253	equivalent to each conjugate coinciding with the subgroup, and the three bridge
254	lemmas make both directions available in the form each client needs.
255	
256	```agda
257	  -- The normality predicate: closure under conjugation, pointwise.
258	  IsNormal : Pred 𝕌[ 𝑮 ] ℓ → Type (α ⊔ ℓ)
259	  IsNormal B = ∀ g {x} → x ∈ B → x ^ g ∈ B
260	
261	  -- For a respecting subset, normality bounds every conjugate above by B ...
262	  normal-conjugate-⊆ : {B : Pred 𝕌[ 𝑮 ] ℓ}
263	    →  B Respects _≈_ → IsNormal B → ∀ g → [ B ]^ g ⊆ B
264	  normal-conjugate-⊆ resp nrmB g (h , h∈B , x≈c) = resp (≈sym x≈c) (nrmB g h∈B)
265	
266	  -- ... and below by B (this direction needs no respect hypothesis) ...
267	  normal-⊆-conjugate : {B : Pred 𝕌[ 𝑮 ] ℓ} → IsNormal B → ∀ g → B ⊆ [ B ]^ g
268	  normal-⊆-conjugate nrmB g {x} x∈B = x ^ (g ⁻¹) , nrmB (g ⁻¹) x∈B , ≈sym (conj-conj⁻¹ g x)
269	
270	  -- ... and conversely, a subset above all of its conjugates is normal.
271	  conjugate-⊆-normal : {B : Pred 𝕌[ 𝑮 ] ℓ} → (∀ g → [ B ]^ g ⊆ B) → IsNormal B
272	  conjugate-⊆-normal cnj g x∈B = cnj g (mem-conjugate g x∈B)
273	
274	  -- The trivial subgroup and the full subgroup are normal.
275	  trivialSubgroupIsnormal : IsNormal (trivialSubgroup 𝒢 .proj₁)
276	  trivialSubgroupIsnormal g x≈ε = ≈trans (conj-cong g x≈ε) (conj-ε g)
277	
278	  fullSubgroupIsnormal : (ℓ : Level) → IsNormal (proj₁ (fullSubgroup 𝒢 ℓ))
279	  fullSubgroupIsnormal ℓ _ _ = lift _
280	```

   bridge lemmas `normal-conjugate-⊆`{.AgdaFunction} and
   `normal-⊆-conjugate`{.AgdaFunction} recover the equivalent formulation "every
   conjugate of `B` coincides with `B`" when `B` respects the equality.

cancellation laws (`\\-leftDividesʳ` and friends) come from the standard library's
`Algebra.Properties.Group`{.AgdaModule} applied to the bundle view
`⟨ 𝑮 ⟩ᵍᵖ`{.AgdaFunction} of [Classical.Bundles.Group][], which is what the bundle

#### Conjugation of elements

`Conj 𝑮` packages conjugation in the group `𝑮`; opening it puts `conj`{.AgdaFunction}
and its algebra of laws in scope.  The laws say: conjugation by a fixed `g` is a group
endomorphism (`conj-ε`{.AgdaFunction}, `conj-∙-hom`{.AgdaFunction},
`conj-⁻¹`{.AgdaFunction}), and as `g` varies it is a left action of the group on
itself (`conj-action-ε`{.AgdaFunction}, `conj-action-∙`{.AgdaFunction}) by
≈-automorphisms (`conj-cong`{.AgdaFunction}, with `conj-conj⁻¹`{.AgdaFunction} and
`conj⁻¹-conj`{.AgdaFunction} the two inverse laws).

```agda
module Conjugate {α ρ : Level} (𝒢@(𝑮 , eqns) : Group α ρ) where

  open Setoid 𝔻[ 𝑮 ]  using ( _≈_ )
                      renaming ( refl to ≈refl ; sym to ≈sym ; trans to ≈trans )
  open SetoidReasoning 𝔻[ 𝑮 ]
  open Group-Op 𝒢 using ( _∙_ ; ε ; _⁻¹ ; ∙-cong ; ⁻¹-cong
                        ; assoc-law ; idˡ-law ; idʳ-law ; invˡ-law ; invʳ-law )
  open GroupProperties ⟨ 𝒢 ⟩ᵍᵖ
    using ( ε⁻¹≈ε ; ⁻¹-involutive ; ⁻¹-anti-homo-∙ ; \\-leftDividesʳ )

  -- Conjugation of the element x by the element g.
  conj : 𝕌[ 𝑮 ] → 𝕌[ 𝑮 ] → 𝕌[ 𝑮 ]
  conj g x = g ∙ x ∙ g ⁻¹

  infixl 30 conj-syntax

  conj-syntax : 𝕌[ 𝑮 ] → 𝕌[ 𝑮 ] → 𝕌[ 𝑮 ]
  conj-syntax = conj

  syntax conj-syntax g x = x ^ g

  -- Conjugation is a congruence in the conjugated element ...
  conj-cong : ∀ g {x y} → x ≈ y → x ^ g ≈ y ^ g
  conj-cong g x≈y = ∙-cong (∙-cong ≈refl x≈y) ≈refl

  -- ... and in the conjugating element.
  conj-congᵍ : ∀ {g h} x → g ≈ h → x ^ g ≈ x ^ h
  conj-congᵍ x g≈h = ∙-cong (∙-cong g≈h ≈refl) (⁻¹-cong g≈h)

  -- Conjugation fixes the identity element.
  conj-ε : ∀ g → ε ^ g  ≈ ε
  conj-ε g = begin
    g ∙ ε ∙ g ⁻¹  ≈⟨ ∙-cong (idʳ-law g) ≈refl ⟩
    g ∙ g ⁻¹      ≈⟨ invʳ-law g ⟩
    ε             ∎

  -- Conjugation by g is multiplicative.
  conj-∙-hom : ∀ g x y → (x ∙ y) ^ g ≈ (x ^ g) ∙ (y ^ g)
  conj-∙-hom g x y = begin
    (x ∙ y) ^ g                        ≈˘⟨ ∙-cong (assoc-law g x y) ≈refl ⟩
    g ∙ x ∙ y ∙ g ⁻¹                   ≈⟨ assoc-law (g ∙ x) y (g ⁻¹) ⟩
    g ∙ x ∙ (y ∙ g ⁻¹)                 ≈˘⟨ ∙-cong ≈refl (\\-leftDividesʳ g (y ∙ g ⁻¹)) ⟩
    g ∙ x ∙ (g ⁻¹ ∙ (g ∙ (y ∙ g ⁻¹)))  ≈˘⟨ ∙-cong ≈refl (∙-cong ≈refl (assoc-law g y (g ⁻¹))) ⟩
    g ∙ x ∙ (g ⁻¹ ∙ (y ^ g))           ≈˘⟨ assoc-law (g ∙ x) (g ⁻¹) (y ^ g) ⟩
    (x ^ g) ∙ (y ^ g)                  ∎

  -- Conjugation by g commutes with inversion.
  conj-⁻¹ : ∀ g x → (x ⁻¹) ^ g ≈ (x ^ g) ⁻¹
  conj-⁻¹ g x = begin
    (x ⁻¹) ^ g              ≈⟨ assoc-law g (x ⁻¹) (g ⁻¹) ⟩
    g ∙ (x ⁻¹ ∙ g ⁻¹)       ≈˘⟨ ∙-cong (⁻¹-involutive g) (⁻¹-anti-homo-∙ g x) ⟩
    (g ⁻¹) ⁻¹ ∙ (g ∙ x) ⁻¹  ≈˘⟨ ⁻¹-anti-homo-∙ (g ∙ x) (g ⁻¹) ⟩
    (x ^ g) ⁻¹ ∎

  -- Varying the conjugator: conjugation is a left action of the group on itself.
  conj-action-∙ : ∀ g h x → x ^ (g ∙ h) ≈ (x ^ h) ^ g
  conj-action-∙ g h x = begin
    x ^ (g ∙ h)                ≈⟨ ≈refl ⟩
    g ∙ h ∙ x ∙ (g ∙ h) ⁻¹     ≈⟨ ∙-cong ≈refl (⁻¹-anti-homo-∙ g h) ⟩
    g ∙ h ∙ x ∙ (h ⁻¹ ∙ g ⁻¹)  ≈˘⟨ assoc-law (g ∙ h ∙ x) (h ⁻¹) (g ⁻¹) ⟩
    g ∙ h ∙ x ∙ h ⁻¹ ∙ g ⁻¹    ≈⟨ ∙-cong (∙-cong (assoc-law g h x) ≈refl) ≈refl ⟩
    g ∙ (h ∙ x) ∙ h ⁻¹ ∙ g ⁻¹  ≈⟨ ∙-cong (assoc-law g (h ∙ x) (h ⁻¹)) ≈refl ⟩
    g ∙ (h ∙ x ∙ h ⁻¹) ∙ g ⁻¹  ≈⟨ ≈refl ⟩
    (x ^ h) ^ g  ∎

  conj-action-ε : ∀ x → x ^ ε ≈ x
  conj-action-ε x = begin
    ε ∙ x ∙ ε ⁻¹  ≈⟨ ∙-cong (idˡ-law x) ε⁻¹≈ε ⟩
    x ∙ ε         ≈⟨ idʳ-law x ⟩
    x             ∎

  -- Conjugating by g undoes conjugating by g ⁻¹, and vice versa.
  conj-conj⁻¹ : ∀ g x → x ^ (g ⁻¹) ^ g ≈ x
  conj-conj⁻¹ g x = begin
    x ^ (g ⁻¹) ^ g    ≈˘⟨ conj-action-∙ g (g ⁻¹) x ⟩
    x ^ (g ∙ g ⁻¹)    ≈⟨ conj-congᵍ x (invʳ-law g) ⟩
    x ^ ε             ≈⟨ conj-action-ε x ⟩
    x                 ∎

  conj⁻¹-conj : ∀ g x → x ^ g ^ (g ⁻¹) ≈ x
  conj⁻¹-conj g x = begin
    x ^ g ^ (g ⁻¹)  ≈˘⟨ conj-action-∙ (g ⁻¹) g x ⟩
    x ^ (g ⁻¹ ∙ g)  ≈⟨ conj-congᵍ x (invˡ-law g) ⟩
    x ^ ε           ≈⟨ conj-action-ε x ⟩
    x               ∎
```

#### Conjugation of subgroups

The conjugate of a subset `B` by `g` is the ≈-saturated image of `B` under
`conj g`{.AgdaFunction}.  It respects the setoid equality by construction, and is a
subuniverse whenever `B` is (via the endomorphism laws above), so conjugation maps
subgroups to subgroups.

```agda
  -- The conjugate subset g B g⁻¹.
  conjugate : 𝕌[ 𝑮 ] → Pred 𝕌[ 𝑮 ] ℓ → Pred 𝕌[ 𝑮 ] (α ⊔ ρ ⊔ ℓ)
  conjugate g B x = ∃[ h ] (h ∈ B × x ≈ h ^ g)

  infixl 30 conjugate-syntax

  conjugate-syntax : 𝕌[ 𝑮 ] → Pred 𝕌[ 𝑮 ] ℓ → Pred 𝕌[ 𝑮 ] (α ⊔ ρ ⊔ ℓ)
  conjugate-syntax = conjugate

  syntax conjugate-syntax g B = [ B ]^ g

  -- The conjugate respects the setoid equality, with no hypothesis on B.
  conjugate-respects : ∀ g (B : Pred 𝕌[ 𝑮 ] ℓ) → [ B ]^ g Respects _≈_
  conjugate-respects g B x≈y (h , h∈B , x≈c) = h , h∈B , ≈trans (≈sym x≈y) x≈c

  -- Conjugation of an element lands in the conjugate of any subset containing it.
  mem-conjugate : ∀ g {B : Pred 𝕌[ 𝑮 ] ℓ} {x} → x ∈ B → x ^ g ∈ [ B ]^ g
  mem-conjugate g x∈B = _ , x∈B , ≈refl

  -- Conjugation of subsets is monotone.
  conjugate-mono : ∀ g {B : Pred 𝕌[ 𝑮 ] ℓ} {C : Pred 𝕌[ 𝑮 ] ℓ'} → B ⊆ C → [ B ]^ g ⊆ [ C ]^ g
  conjugate-mono g B⊆C (h , h∈B , x≈c) = h , B⊆C h∈B , x≈c

  -- The conjugate of a subuniverse is a subuniverse.
  conjugate-isSubuniverse : (g : 𝕌[ 𝑮 ]) (B : Pred 𝕌[ 𝑮 ] ℓ)
    →  B ∈ Subuniverses 𝑮 → [ B ]^ g ∈ Subuniverses 𝑮
  conjugate-isSubuniverse g B B-sub ∙-Op a im =
    h₀ ∙ h₁ , sub-∙-closed 𝒢 B B-sub h₀∈B h₁∈B , eq
    where
    h₀ h₁ : 𝕌[ 𝑮 ]
    h₀ = im 0F .proj₁
    h₁ = im 1F .proj₁

    h₀∈B : h₀ ∈ B
    h₀∈B = im 0F .proj₂ .proj₁

    h₁∈B : h₁ ∈ B
    h₁∈B = im 1F .proj₂ .proj₁

    eq : (∙-Op ̂  𝑮) a ≈ (h₀ ∙ h₁) ^ g
    eq = begin
      (∙-Op ̂  𝑮) a      ≈⟨ interp-tuple-∙ 𝒢 a ⟩
      a 0F ∙ a 1F       ≈⟨ ∙-cong (im 0F .proj₂ .proj₂) (im 1F .proj₂ .proj₂) ⟩
      h₀ ^ g ∙ h₁ ^ g   ≈˘⟨ conj-∙-hom g h₀ h₁ ⟩
      (h₀ ∙ h₁) ^ g     ∎

  conjugate-isSubuniverse g B B-sub ε-Op a im = ε , sub-ε-closed 𝒢 B B-sub , eq
    where
    eq : (ε-Op ̂  𝑮) a ≈ ε ^ g
    eq = begin
      (ε-Op ̂  𝑮) a  ≈⟨ interp-tuple-ε 𝒢 a ⟩
      ε             ≈˘⟨ conj-ε g ⟩
      ε ^ g         ∎

  conjugate-isSubuniverse g B B-sub ⁻¹-Op a im = h ⁻¹ , sub-⁻¹-closed 𝒢 B B-sub h∈B , eq
    where
    h : 𝕌[ 𝑮 ]
    h = im 0F .proj₁

    h∈B : h ∈ B
    h∈B = im 0F .proj₂ .proj₁

    eq : (⁻¹-Op ̂  𝑮) a ≈ (h ⁻¹) ^ g
    eq = begin
      (⁻¹-Op ̂  𝑮) a  ≈⟨ interp-tuple-⁻¹ 𝒢 a ⟩
      a 0F ⁻¹        ≈⟨ ⁻¹-cong (im 0F .proj₂ .proj₂) ⟩
      (h ^ g) ⁻¹     ≈˘⟨ conj-⁻¹ g h ⟩
      (h ⁻¹) ^ g     ∎
```

#### The normality predicate

A subset is **normal** when it is closed under conjugation by every group element.
The property is stated for bare predicates; for ≈-respecting subgroups it is
equivalent to each conjugate coinciding with the subgroup, and the three bridge
lemmas make both directions available in the form each client needs.

```agda
  -- The normality predicate: closure under conjugation, pointwise.
  IsNormal : Pred 𝕌[ 𝑮 ] ℓ → Type (α ⊔ ℓ)
  IsNormal B = ∀ g {x} → x ∈ B → x ^ g ∈ B

  -- For a respecting subset, normality bounds every conjugate above by B ...
  normal-conjugate-⊆ : {B : Pred 𝕌[ 𝑮 ] ℓ}
    →  B Respects _≈_ → IsNormal B → ∀ g → [ B ]^ g ⊆ B
  normal-conjugate-⊆ resp nrmB g (h , h∈B , x≈c) = resp (≈sym x≈c) (nrmB g h∈B)

  -- ... and below by B (this direction needs no respect hypothesis) ...
  normal-⊆-conjugate : {B : Pred 𝕌[ 𝑮 ] ℓ} → IsNormal B → ∀ g → B ⊆ [ B ]^ g
  normal-⊆-conjugate nrmB g {x} x∈B = x ^ (g ⁻¹) , nrmB (g ⁻¹) x∈B , ≈sym (conj-conj⁻¹ g x)

  -- ... and conversely, a subset above all of its conjugates is normal.
  conjugate-⊆-normal : {B : Pred 𝕌[ 𝑮 ] ℓ} → (∀ g → [ B ]^ g ⊆ B) → IsNormal B
  conjugate-⊆-normal cnj g x∈B = cnj g (mem-conjugate g x∈B)

  -- The trivial subgroup and the full subgroup are normal.
  trivialSubgroupIsnormal : IsNormal (trivialSubgroup 𝒢 .proj₁)
  trivialSubgroupIsnormal g x≈ε = ≈trans (conj-cong g x≈ε) (conj-ε g)

  fullSubgroupIsnormal : (ℓ : Level) → IsNormal (proj₁ (fullSubgroup 𝒢 ℓ))
  fullSubgroupIsnormal ℓ _ _ = lift _
```

```agda
  (P ∙ᶜ Q) x = Σ[ p ∈ G ] Σ[ q ∈ G ] (p ∈ P × q ∈ Q × x ≈ p ∙ q)

  -- A literal product of members is a member of the complex product.
  mem-∙ᶜ : {P : Pred G ℓ} {Q : Pred G ℓ'} {p q : G}
    →  p ∈ P → q ∈ Q → p ∙ q ∈ P ∙ᶜ Q
  mem-∙ᶜ p∈P q∈Q = _ , _ , p∈P , q∈Q , ≈refl

  -- The complex product respects the setoid equality, with no hypotheses on P, Q.
  ∙ᶜ-respects : (P : Pred G ℓ) (Q : Pred G ℓ') → (P ∙ᶜ Q) Respects _≈_
  ∙ᶜ-respects P Q {x} {y} x≈y (p , q , p∈P , q∈Q , x≈pq) = p , q , p∈P , q∈Q , y≈pq
    where
    y≈pq : y ≈ p ∙ q
    y≈pq = ≈trans (≈sym x≈y) x≈pq

  -- The complex product is monotone in both arguments.  (The four predicates are
  -- given independent levels: consumers routinely enlarge a product of two
  -- small-level factors into a single subgroup at another level.)
  ∙ᶜ-mono : {P : Pred G ℓ} {P' : Pred G ℓ₁} {Q : Pred G ℓ'} {Q' : Pred G ℓ₂}
    →  P ⊆ P' → Q ⊆ Q' → P ∙ᶜ Q ⊆ P' ∙ᶜ Q'
  ∙ᶜ-mono P⊆P' Q⊆Q' (p , q , p∈P , q∈Q , x≈pq) =
    p , q , P⊆P' p∈P , Q⊆Q' q∈Q , x≈pq
```

#### Subgroups absorb their own complex square

For a subgroup `H` the complex product `H H` collapses back to `H`: one inclusion
is closure under `∙` (plus respect), the other writes `x` as `x ∙ ε`.  This is the
prototypical use of the toolkit and a lemma the interval arguments reuse.

```agda
  subgroup-∙ᶜ-idem : {H : Pred G ℓ} → IsSubgroup 𝒢 H → (H ∙ᶜ H) ≐ H
  subgroup-∙ᶜ-idem {H = H} H-isSubgroup = below , above
    where
    open IsSubgroup H-isSubgroup using ( respects ; ∙-closed ; ε-closed )

    below : H ∙ᶜ H ⊆ H
    below (p , q , p∈H , q∈H , x≈pq) = respects (≈sym x≈pq) (∙-closed p∈H q∈H)

    above : H ⊆ H ∙ᶜ H
    above {x} x∈H = x , ε , x∈H , ε-closed , ≈sym (idʳ-law x)
```

---

[^1] The role played by `_∙ᶜ_`{.AgdaFunction} in this development is as the
     vocabulary of **Dedekind's rule** (`A ≤ B → A(C ∩ B) = AC ∩ B`, in
     [Classical.Structures.Group.Dedekind][]) and, downstream, of the
     permuting-complement and parachute arguments of the FLRP research program
     (`docs/notes/flrp-research-roadmap.md` § 4).

#### The trivial and full subgroups

The trivial subgroup is the ≈-class of the identity, `{ x ∣ x ≈ ε }`; over a setoid
carrier the *class*, not the syntactic singleton, is the right notion.  The full
subgroup is the whole carrier.

```agda
  fullSubgroup : (ℓ : Level) → Subgroup ℓ
  fullSubgroup ℓ =  (λ _ → Lift ℓ ⊤)
```
